paragraphs.source_en: what object for his strong passions—had he sought there? I dared not answer the question. Oh, my poor master— once almost my husband—whom I had often called ‘my dear Edward!’ ‘He must have been a bad man,’ observed Mr. Rivers. ‘You don’t know him—don’t pronounce an opinion upon him,’ I said, with warmth. ‘Very well,’ he answered quietly: ‘and indeed my head is otherwise occupied than with him: I have my tale to finish. Since you won’t ask the governess’s name, I must tell it of my own accord. Stay! I have it here—it is always more satisfactory to see important points written down, fairly committed to black and white.’
